Educational material only. This is not investment, tax or legal advice, and it does not recommend any product. Nothing here was acted on: no account was opened, no funds moved, no brokerage or bank was contacted.

## How to read the status labels

- Verified: stated by a page I could retrieve on 2026-11-24, with the URL in parentheses. Several pages were read through the WebFetch tool, which returns a summary of the page rather than raw text; where a page itself was blocked (Cloudflare or HTTP 403) the fact comes from search-result text and is labelled as such.
- Reported: appears in third-party reviews or search summaries, not on a primary page I could retrieve. Treat as a lead.
- UNVERIFIED - confirm in app: no live source found, or the claim was supplied by John and could not be confirmed or refuted from public pages.

## Verified facts about Uphold equities

### Availability and launch

- Uphold announced single-step crypto-to-equities trading on July 21, 2026, covering "more than 4,000 leading U.S. stocks and ETFs" (https://crypto.news/uphold-launches-single-step-crypto-to-equities-trading-for-4000-u-s-stocks-and-etfs/).
- Jurisdiction: the equities page says "U.S. only. Additional onboarding required." (https://uphold.com/en-us/equities). A search summary stated that Louisiana, New York and U.S. territories are excluded, but I could not retrieve a primary page saying so. State-level eligibility is therefore UNVERIFIED - confirm in app.
- Hours: during the beta launch, orders are accepted 9:30 am to 4:00 pm ET, Monday to Friday, with 24-hours-a-day, five-days-a-week trading listed as "coming soon" (https://uphold.com/en-us/equities).
- The shares are traditional U.S. equities and ETFs, not tokenized securities (https://uphold.com/en-us/equities).
- A third-party page in the search results claimed that Uphold does not support stock trading. That conflicts with Uphold's own pages and the July 2026 launch coverage, and I treat it as stale.

### Crypto to USD to stock: the conversion flow

- Per the launch coverage: "cryptocurrency will first be converted into U.S. Dollars by Uphold HQ, Inc.," and the proceeds then move "to their brokerage account at Uphold Securities Corp." The customer places one order and the app performs both legs (https://crypto.news/uphold-launches-single-step-crypto-to-equities-trading-for-4000-u-s-stocks-and-etfs/; https://uphold.com/en-us/equities). The entity named differs between sources (Uphold Securities Inc. on Uphold's own pages, Uphold Securities Corp. in the quoted release text); confirm the legal name on your account documents.
- Two legal entities are involved: Uphold HQ Inc. handles the crypto leg and Uphold Securities Inc. the brokerage leg (https://crypto.news/uphold-launches-single-step-crypto-to-equities-trading-for-4000-u-s-stocks-and-etfs/).
- Fractional shares are supported, with a $5 minimum "subject to account approval" (https://crypto.news/uphold-launches-single-step-crypto-to-equities-trading-for-4000-u-s-stocks-and-etfs/).

### Account opening

- Steps stated on Uphold's page: a verified Uphold account, then Equities on the app's home screen, "Start investing", and answer a few onboarding questions to establish a self-directed Equities account (https://uphold.com/en-us/equities).
- A search summary listed further requirements (age 18 or over, a matching SSN or TIN, residence in a supported state). The primary page I could retrieve did not list them; treat as Reported and confirm in the app.
- Uphold's support article "Get started with Equities" (https://support.uphold.com/hc/en-us/articles/53122698072859-Get-started-with-Equities) returned a Cloudflare challenge to every automated fetch, so I could not read it.

### Fees and spreads

- Equities: "0% commission on cash-to-stock & ETF trades" with the note "Other fees and charges may apply"; crypto-to-stock conversions carry exchange fees plus brokerage fees (https://uphold.com/en-us/equities). The securities fee schedule lists $0.00 commissions on equity trades including fractional shares, $0.00 for account opening, maintenance, inactivity and closing, and notes that SEC and FINRA regulatory fees still apply to sales (https://uphold.com/legal/security-disclosures).
- Crypto leg: Uphold's fee page says every trade, sale or conversion carries a "spread" built into the quoted price, determined by the asset, the trade size, market conditions and volatility, liquidity cost and network costs. It does not publish a spread rate in the retrieved text (https://uphold.com/en-us/get-started/service-fees). Third-party reviews report spreads of up to 1.6% for Bitcoin and Ether and up to 2.95% for altcoins (Reported, not confirmed; e.g. https://cryptoslate.com/crypto-exchanges/uphold-exchange-review/). The all-in price should be on the in-app preview before you confirm. Whether the preview shows the spread separately is UNVERIFIED - confirm in app.

### Transfers and ACATS

- Transfers out: $100 for a full or partial ACATS transfer out (https://uphold.com/legal/security-disclosures).
- Search results, summarising Uphold's support content, state that fractional positions are generally liquidated to cash before an ACAT transfer. I could not retrieve the support page. Reported; confirm in app.
- ACATS transfers in (moving shares from another broker to Uphold): UNVERIFIED - confirm in app.
- Wires, ACH and checks are listed with no customer charge ("n/a") on the Uphold Securities fee schedule (https://uphold.com/legal/security-disclosures).

### Protection

- Securities and cash held at Apex Clearing carry SIPC coverage "up to $500,000, including up to $250,000 for cash." Funds in the Uphold account itself "are not held in your brokerage account and are not protected by SIPC" (https://uphold.com/legal/security-disclosures). That second sentence matters for the crypto leg: crypto sits outside the brokerage account until converted.

## A step-by-step outline (educational)

1. Confirm eligibility in the app or the support site before depositing anything: country, state, and age and tax-identification requirements. State-level exclusions are UNVERIFIED here.
2. Install the Uphold app from the official store listing and complete identity verification (the Uphold account is a prerequisite for Equities).
3. Fund the Uphold account with crypto (deposit address from the app) or USD. Check the network and token before sending; a wrong-network deposit may not be recoverable. Whether a given token is supported for the equity swap is UNVERIFIED - confirm in app.
4. Open Equities ("Start investing") and complete onboarding for the self-directed account.
5. Place the single-step order: choose the crypto to sell and the stock or ETF to buy. Read the preview for the exchange rate, any spread and any fees before confirming. Orders are limited to 9:30 to 16:00 ET on market days at present.
6. Record the transaction details. In the U.S., selling or converting crypto is generally treated as a disposal for tax purposes. That is general information, not from Uphold; ask a tax professional.
7. To leave: ACATS out costs $100 (verified above); selling to cash and withdrawing is the alternative.

### Fit with the trading harness

The harness notes want API orders if possible. For Uphold equities none was verified, and the supplied claim is that no retail equity API exists. The practical consequence is the harness's own fallback: signal-and-alert, with manual limit orders in the app. A limit-order workflow is not verified either; the pages read mention orders but not order types (UNVERIFIED - confirm in app).

### The two-hop route: exchange, bank, then broker

Sell the crypto on an exchange for USD, withdraw by ACH or wire to a bank account, then fund an established broker by ACH or wire. Compared with a direct swap it adds days of settlement and one more counterparty, and it keeps the crypto sale and the stock purchase as separate, visible steps. In exchange for that friction it unlocks brokers with documented trading APIs, such as Alpaca (a documented individual Trading API, per the page above). Whether any specific bank or exchange is suitable is outside what I verified.

### Reading the table for the harness

- If API orders are a hard requirement, the verified candidates are Alpaca (documented Trading API, ACH and wire funding) and, if its API pages are confirmed, Interactive Brokers (stablecoin funding reported, API unverified). Uphold, Coinbase and Kraken have no verified equities API.
- If keeping the crypto leg and the stock leg in one place matters more than automation, Uphold and Coinbase are the verified integrated paths.
- Spreads and fees differ materially by leg; compare the all-in preview, not the commission line.

## Appendix

### The four-stock equilibrium strategy: weights from shares outstanding and market capitalization

Educational analysis, not investment advice. The numbers are from this week's data; the $10,000 is an illustrative notional.

### Inputs

Shares outstanding, as supplied in the brief: AVGO 4.77B; Alphabet 12,280,813,656 (all classes, valued at the GOOG price, which is an approximation because share classes trade at different prices); META 2.56B; SNAP 1.718B. Closes are Yahoo daily bars (https://query1.finance.yahoo.com/v8/finance/chart/) saved in `data/`; computation in `scripts/08_strategy.R`.

| Stock | Shares (B) | Share-count proportion | Thu close | Fri close | Mon close | Cap Fri $B | Cap-share weight Thu | Cap-share weight Fri | Cap-share weight Mon |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| AVGO | 4.770 | 22.36% | 346.65 | 304.41 | 313.55 | 1,452.0 | 25.37% | 23.66% | 23.13% |
| GOOG | 12.281 | 57.58% | 271.02 | 264.00 | 279.53 | 3,242.1 | 51.07% | 52.82% | 53.08% |
| META | 2.560 | 12.00% | 596.22 | 560.84 | 597.60 | 1,435.8 | 23.42% | 23.39% | 23.66% |
| SNAP | 1.718 | 8.05% | 5.12 | 4.55 | 4.92 | 7.8 | 0.13% | 0.13% | 0.13% |

### Two readings of "the ratio of shares outstanding to total market capitalization"

Reading (a), capitalization share: weight_i = (shares_i x price_i) / sum over the four of (shares_j x price_j). It depends on price, so it moves every time prices move. Note the combined capitalization of the four is $6,517B on Thursday, $6,138B on Friday and $6,467B on Monday (R-computed, same script). The weights above are this reading.

Reading (b), share-count proportion: weight_i = shares_i / sum of shares_j. It ignores price entirely and never changes. Alphabet's 12.28B shares make it 57.58% of the four by count (against 51.07% by capitalization on Thursday), while SNAP, at 1.718B shares of a stock near $5, would get 8.05% of the weight despite being 0.13% of the combined capitalization:

| Stock | Share-count proportion (fixed, as a target weight) | Cap-share weight Thu | Cap-share weight Mon | Move in cap-share weight Thu->Mon (pp) | Move in share-count proportion (pp) |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| AVGO | 22.36% | 25.37% | 23.13% | -2.24 | +0.00 |
| GOOG | 57.58% | 51.07% | 53.08% | +2.01 | +0.00 |
| META | 12.00% | 23.42% | 23.66% | +0.24 | +0.00 |
| SNAP | 8.05% | 0.13% | 0.13% | -0.00 | +0.00 |

Why (b) fails the "modulates toward equilibrium" requirement: a price-insensitive weight cannot respond to anything. Used as a target weight it is a fixed vector, so rebalancing toward it produces trades that depend on the investor's own history rather than on the market, and it overweights SNAP roughly 60-fold relative to its cap share (8.05% against about 0.13%). Used as quantities (hold shares in the ratio 4.77 : 12.28 : 2.56 : 1.718) it is exactly buy-and-hold of the cap-weighted basket: values then always equal cap shares by construction, and no trade is ever called for. Neither gives a feedback loop.

Reading (a) as a target is the coherent one: set the target to the cap-share vector at a reference date, let prices move, and trade back toward the target when a weight drifts beyond a band. That is the drift-band constant-mix already sketched in the harness notes (CONTEXT.md, section 3), with the target now defined by capitalization instead of an ad hoc 25/25/50 split. "Equilibrium" here is a modelling assumption, not a finding: it assumes that relative capitalization shares mean-revert, so that selling the relative winners and buying the relative losers is rewarded on average. Nothing in this week's data tests that.

### Worked example

Target: Thursday Nov 19 close cap shares (25.37% AVGO, 51.07% GOOG, 23.42% META, 0.13% SNAP). Notional $10,000 at the Thursday close. Check once a day at the close (harness rule). Trigger: absolute weight drift of at least 4 or 5 percentage points. Fractional shares are assumed for illustration.

| Stock | Check | Value $ | Weight | Target | Drift (pp) | Trade that would restore target $ (not triggered) |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| AVGO | Fri | 2,228.08 | 23.66% | 25.37% | -1.71 | +161.52 |
| GOOG | Fri | 4,974.90 | 52.82% | 51.07% | +1.75 | -164.92 |
| META | Fri | 2,203.09 | 23.39% | 23.42% | -0.03 | +2.69 |
| SNAP | Fri | 11.99 | 0.13% | 0.13% | -0.01 | +0.72 |
| AVGO | Mon | 2,294.98 | 23.13% | 25.37% | -2.24 | +222.73 |
| GOOG | Mon | 5,267.55 | 53.08% | 51.07% | +2.01 | -199.70 |
| META | Mon | 2,347.49 | 23.66% | 23.42% | +0.24 | -23.46 |
| SNAP | Mon | 12.97 | 0.13% | 0.13% | -0.00 | +0.42 |

The check on Friday, after AVGO fell 12.19%, shows a maximum drift of 1.75 percentage points; on Monday, 2.24. Neither the 4pp nor the 5pp trigger fires, so the rule calls for no trade; the right-hand column shows what a trade would have been. The reason is arithmetic: all four stocks fell together, and a 25% weight needs the stock to outperform the rest by a large margin to drift 5pp:

| Stock | Weight (Thu) | Rise vs rest for +4pp drift | Rise vs rest for +5pp drift | Fall vs rest for -5pp drift |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| AVGO | 25.37% | +22.3% | +28.3% | -24.7% |
| GOOG | 51.07% | +17.4% | +22.3% | -18.2% |
| META | 23.42% | +23.5% | +29.8% | -26.2% |
| SNAP | 0.13% | +3091.4% | +3905.0% | not reachable (weight below 5%) |

Starting the target from the Friday close instead shows an even smaller Monday drift:

| Stock | Target (Fri close cap share) | Weight at Mon close | Drift (pp) | Trade that would restore target $ (not triggered) |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| AVGO | 23.66% | 23.13% | -0.53 | +55.80 |
| GOOG | 52.82% | 53.08% | +0.26 | -27.54 |
| META | 23.39% | 23.66% | +0.26 | -27.91 |
| SNAP | 0.13% | 0.13% | +0.00 | -0.35 |

A hypothetical in which the trigger does fire (AVGO +30% against the other three flat; this is an illustration, not data):

| Stock | Start $ | Hypothetical value $ | Weight | Target | Drift (pp) | Trigger at 5pp | Rebalance trade $ |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| AVGO | 2,537.25 | 3,298.42 | 30.65% | 25.37% | +5.28 | yes | -568.05 |
| GOOG | 5,107.19 | 5,107.19 | 47.46% | 51.07% | -3.61 | no | +388.75 |
| META | 2,342.07 | 2,342.07 | 21.76% | 23.42% | -1.66 | no | +178.27 |
| SNAP | 13.50 | 13.50 | 0.13% | 0.13% | -0.01 | no | +1.03 |

In that scenario the rule sells about $568 of AVGO and buys about $389 of GOOG, $178 of META and $1 of SNAP, restoring the target weights. Two consequences worth stating plainly. First, on this basket and with a 5pp band the strategy trades rarely: it is a slow rebalancer, not a signal generator. Second, cap-share weights put 53% of the capital in one stock (Alphabet, whose capitalization here uses all share classes at the GOOG price) and almost nothing in SNAP, so the practical portfolio is a three-stock one; the harness's choice to exclude SNAP is consistent with the arithmetic (three-stock weights on Thursday: 25.41%, 51.14%, 23.45%).

### Where the equilibrium assumption is fragile

- Regime shifts: a rebalancer trades against moves. If a Friday-style repricing is a permanent re-rating of one member, selling relative winners and buying relative losers works against the new level. The AVGO path (22% of Friday's drop retraced; a Tuesday snapshot back at Friday's close) is the kind of case where the question is open.
- Gaps: both days' moves arrived mostly overnight (Monday's gaps were 84% to 180% of close-over-close moves for the four stocks and Nvidia; see the companion document). A once-a-day, at-the-close check cannot act inside a gap.
- Volatility and rates: the harness gauge (VIX under 30 and the 10-year under 5% is "contained"; VIX 30 to 40 or a 10-year at or above 5% is "boiling": widen bands, halve size; above 40 is "flashing": no rebalancing) put Friday's close (VIX 35.89) in the boiling band and Monday's (VIX 26.62; 10-year 4.918%) in the contained band. On Friday, VIX traded as high as 40.03 intraday.
- Correlation: the basket fell together on Friday and rose together on Monday, so within-basket drift stayed under 2.3pp. The band diversifies little when the common factor dominates.
- Costs: trade sizes at $10,000 notional are in the tens to low hundreds of dollars; on a venue with crypto spreads of 1.6% or more on the funding leg, round-trip costs can exceed the small rebalancing benefit. Spread levels are Reported, not confirmed.
- Disclosure: educational analysis, not investment advice. Past prices do not predict future prices, and nothing here tests whether the strategy would have been profitable.
